subject: Post-demo: prioritized model slate and recommended next steps for Lumos Assist
messages:
From: Ana Guerrero <ana@lumos.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood demo — recommended models & next steps

Markus — thanks again for the demo today. The team liked the latency numbers and the fact you showed both hosted and dedicated options. A couple quick context points to make sure our asks are aligned: we're evaluating for Lumos Assist (customer support summarization + contextual suggestions). Target SLOs: 99th perc latency < 120ms p95 around 70ms for short summaries (avg output ~120 tokens). Target unit cost: ideally <= $0.04 per 1k tokens in hosted, or lower on Dedicated.

We'd like a concise recommended slate of 2–3 models you think are the best fit (one optimistic/high-quality, one balanced, one low-cost/low-latency) plus benchmark links, prompt-set examples, and any regression risks we should watch for. Also please surface deployment mode recommendation (hosted vs dedicated) and whether quantized variants are production-ready for our use case.

Can you send this over by EOD Monday so I can share with engineering + procurement? Procurement may loop in next steps for pricing and SOW.

Thanks,
Ana Guerrero
Head of Product, Lumos AI

--
Lumos AI
ana@lumos.ai

From: markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Guerrero <ana@lumos.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood demo — recommended models & next steps

Ana — appreciated the clear constraints. Quick recap + prioritized slate below (short + actionable). Attached: lumos_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl (sample prompt set), redwood_model_profiles_202702.pdf (Redwood-verified latency/cost profiles), benchmark_summary_lumos_q1.csv (our internal run on your sample corpus).

Priority slate (rationale + expected perf on Redwood Dedicated n1-gpu-optimized pools; hosted numbers slightly higher latency/cost):

1) RW-Instruct-7B-q4 (balanced) — recommended primary
   - Why: Strong instruction-following for summarization and retrieval-augmented responses, good instruction-tuning for short summaries.
   - Latency: ~60–75ms median, 95th ~110–125ms (Dedicated, single-token steady-state for 120-token output).
   - Cost: ~ $0.025 per 1k tokens (quantized q4 path).
   - Quality: High for abstractive summaries; robust to prompt variants.
   - Risk: Degradation if prompt context >> 2k tokens without KV cache optimization; monitor hallucination on rare legal/finance terms.

2) RW-2.7B-rapid (low-latency/low-cost) — recommended fallback/scale path
   - Why: Optimized for throughput and very low latency; great for high-concurrency endpoints.
   - Latency: ~35–55ms median, 95th ~80–95ms.
   - Cost: ~ $0.012–0.015 per 1k tokens.
   - Quality: Good for extractive summaries and short completions; may be less fluent on complex, nuanced summarization.
   - Risk: Might require prompt engineering to hit desired quality on longer context windows.

3) OpenLlama-13B-rlhf (high-quality) — recommended for heavy accuracy/QA lanes (canary/high-importance cases)
   - Why: Better factuality and coherence on longer, more complex threads.
   - Latency: ~140–200ms median on Dedicated (higher on hosted); consider batching and async paths.
   - Cost: ~ $0.06 per 1k tokens (unquantized); quantized builds can reduce cost but require validation.
   - Quality: Best of the three for nuanced summarization and instruction following.
   - Risk: Higher cost/latency; needs stronger regression monitoring for prompt drift.

Deployment recommendation:
- Start with a mixed routing policy: primary RW-Instruct-7B-q4 for standard flows, RW-2.7B-rapid for bulk/low-latency short responses, and OpenLlama-13B as a canary/priority lane for SLAs or high-value customers. Redwood's smart routing can fall back automatically if primary capacity is constrained.

Quantization notes:
- q4 quantized variants (used above) are production-ready for many summarization workloads and give the best cost/latency tradeoff. For OpenLlama-13B we recommend validating q4->q3 transitions in a sandbox; heavy-tail prompts can show subtle differences in factuality.

Monitoring & regression controls we'd put in place initially:
- Prompt-set based quality checks (we ran the attached prompt pack against the three candidates).
- Automated quality regression alerts tied to a small eval set (we suggest 150–200 labelled examples representative of your user queries).
- Token-level cost dashboards and a per-route SLA heatmap (we can provide a dashboard link once onboarded).

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- Tue: Engineering sync (30m) to confirm perf targets and data flows — suggest Tue 2/16 11:00 PT.
- Thu: Procurement + SOW intro (procurement@lumos.ai) — Redwood to share pricing sheet and draft SOW.
- Week of 2/22: Pilot deployment (Dedicated burst pool) + regression monitoring enabled for a 2-week run.

Links & artifacts (attached/linked):
- lumos_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl (attached) — sample prompts we used for benchmarks
- https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/LUMOS-PROMPTS-2027 — prompt pack + eval labels
- redwood_model_profiles_202702.pdf — one-page performance/cost summary for each model
- benchmark_summary_lumos_q1.csv — run results on your sample dataset

I'll loop Ben for the pricing and procurement bits. If this slate looks right, we'll draft the SOW and the pilot configuration.

—Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood demo — recommended models & next steps

Ana / Markus — quick note on regression guardrails and procurement inputs.

1) Quality monitoring: we recommend Redwood Optimize eval harness with these initial triggers:
   - Daily sample drift check (100 random user sessions)
   - Weekly holdout eval against the 200 labelled examples mentioned above
   - Immediate alert on >5% drop in ROUGE-L or human-verified accuracy for high-value tickets

2) Canary policy for OpenLlama-13B: start at 1% of traffic for 48–72h with manual approval gating; if no regression, scale to 10% for a week.

3) Procurement inputs I can share immediately: pricing sheet (on per-token and per-concurrent-endpoint tiers), dedicated burst configurations, and our standard SOW template. I'll attach pricing in the SOW email once we confirm the slate.

I'll also add short instructions to the prompt pack for producing the 200-label eval set from your historical tickets — reduces labelling lift.

-Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
